title: Gatekeeper

validation.research: Four primary sources verified. Microsoft Azure Architecture Center establishes the cloud Gatekeeper pattern: limited-privilege public request validation separated from private business processing and storage authority. OWASP establishes least privilege, deny by default, authorization on every request and safe failure. Python documents input limits and the object-pairs decoder hook. OPA documents its separately named Kubernetes Gatekeeper policy product, which is not an alias for the architecture pattern. No existing exact canonical article found; no additional alias invented. Reference Monitor remains a stronger whole-boundary concept; Facade/Proxy/Bulkhead remain distinct existing patterns. Bulkhead reuses its established canonical data-workload-isolation ID.

example_limits: Bounded behavioral responsibility simulation, not a deployed security boundary. Trusted composition supplies an already verified principal. The fixed callback stands in for an authenticated restricted service channel. Two classes, frozen values and private-field naming provide no process/network isolation, authentication, tamper resistance or storage-credential protection. The sample is a read-only preview, not durable submission/printing, and makes no exactly-once or concurrent transaction guarantee. Real ingestion needs streaming body limits before assembly; real services need current authoritative authorization and operation-specific consistency, capacity/deadline/lifecycle controls. A compromised gatekeeper can abuse its permitted internal capability.
